newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest hogs called mostly $.50-$1 higher - trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest hogs called mostly $.50-$1 higher - trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices were called mostly $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt higher Thursday because a major packer raised bids for hogs late Wednesday, Illinois and Indiana livestock dealers said.
However, Iowa dealers expect steady to weak prices because of expected lower cash pork prices Wednesday.

Illinois and Indiana sources said buyers for a major packer began aggressively bidding for hogs late Wednesday and indicated that demand would continue into Thursday. Illinois had a top price of $52.00 Wednesday and Indiana had an extreme top of $52.50 and practical top of $52.00.
Iowa sources said some hogs scheduled for delivery Thursday were priced steady. They said hog marketings Wednesday appeared to be sufficient to satisfy demand.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota markets were steady Wednesday with an extreme hog top of $53.50 top and practial top of $53.00.
